title: Supply Chain Coordinator-National-Damascus
description: Country: Syrian Arab Republic                                       Organization: Save the Children                                                                       Closing date: 10 Sep 2026                                         TEAM/PROGRAMME: Supply ChainLOCATION: DAMASCUSGRADE: 3DURATION: 6 monthsCHILD SAFEGUARDING: Level 3 – the responsibilities of the post may require the post holder to have regular contact with or access to children or young peopleROLE PURPOSE: The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for managing and coordinating the supply chain operations for the Syria Response Office. This position is designed to ensure the smooth and efficient functioning of both administrative and supply chain processes, which include procurement, logistics, warehousing, inventory management, office administration, and asset management. The role involves and providing support for programmatic needs through procurement, logistics, and general office operations, while ensuring compliance with organizational policies, procedures, and legal requirements.SCOPE OF ROLE: Reports to Head of office,Direct Reports: Supply Chain Officer/sKEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY: Procurement Oversight function in Syria Response office (30%) • Support the head of Supply Chain in effecting Global and Regional Supply Chain Priorities downstream to ensure alignment and implementation of Supply Chain Strategy through compliant, efficient and effective supply chain management mechanisms. • Implement Supply chain strategy to ensure that the supply chain function deliver on program priorities and realise best sourcing outcomes • Implement the SCI Procurement Manual and Country Logistics Manual, Partner Procurement Guidelines and SRO Procurement Policy to ensure highest levels of compliance. • Enforce the application of the SCI legal Memo Compliance with Sanctions & Export Controls • Implement Supply Chain Child Safeguarding Measures / Action Plans • Consolidate the financial benefits derived from procurement transactions as part of meeting SRO target for cost savings / cost avoidance from our supplier spend. • Manage performance of the direct reports and support their respective areas of growth and development • Preparing a capacity building plan for implementing partners and providing the necessary support for the points identified in the plan. • Follow standard preparedness practices to ensure SCI is able to quickly respond and deploy needed resources to affected areas at the onset of the crisis. • Act in an assigned response capacity as required to meet assistance needs. • Develop and update the list of qualified vendors based on the local and international markets. Logistics Coordination-10% • Implement logistics and supply chain standards and procedures /SCI Quality Framework to meet SCI operational quality standards. • Promote the timely development of Distribution Plans from program teams to ensure accurate distribution of supplies within active project life • Implement SCI fleet management systems to ensure accountable, efficient use and allocation of the vehicle fleet. • Coordinate with RPU on International Procurement and freight scheduling whenever required • Oversee the receiving, clearing, and forwarding of all SCI cargo, ensuring that shipments are handled efficiently and in line with SCI protocols. • Take charge of monitoring, tracking, and reporting on all incoming and outgoing shipments, ensuring that goods are delivered to their final destinations without unnecessary delays. • Manage and facilitate customs clearance procedures, ensuring timely processing of shipments while adhering to local customs laws and regulations. • Communicate shipment statuses regularly to key stakeholders, addressing any potential issues such as delays or transportation challenges • Communicate logistics progress and any challenges to internal stakeholders in a timely and effective manner, ensuring that any issues related to shipments or customs clearance are addressed collaboratively. Asset Management – 15% • Oversee the Syria Response asset registers are constantly updated, maintained, that all assets are logged, issued with unique asset numbers and cards and are tracked • Champion the Asset Verification Exercise periodically to ensure an accurate listing of Assets in Syria Response Office. • Monitor the acquisition of assets in close adherence with the BIS or other donor specific requirements. • Oversee key Trackers holding all closeout documentation including asset database, closeout letters, stock donation certificates. Warehousing and Inventory Management – 15% • Lead the process of Quarterly Physical Stock take to ensure records and physical stocks records are reconciled within active project life of awards and grants • Conduct spot checks to Randomly monitor stocks and Program supplies are effectively entered on the Total Inventory Management Systems to account for all inbound and outbound movement of commodities and Program Supplies • Develop and implement a comprehensive work plan for warehouse management in collaboration with the program and field manager. Develop the skills and experience of Save the Children Supply Chain staff (20%) • Coach staff to ensure performance or implementation issues are solved in a consultative manner • Take ownership of personal capacity-building, ensuring plan is in place and agreed with Line Manager in order to build on areas of growth. Information Management-10% • Consolidate, review and submit Monthly reports including Procurement Trackers Tender Tracker, BAF Tracker, Asset Register & KPI Consolidated File and fleet tracker. • Monitor Key Performance Indicators (KPI’s) Metrics to track performance as part of Supply Chain and Programme Quality check The post-holder will comply with all relevant Save the Children policies and procedures with respect to child safeguarding, safety and security, code of conduct, equal opportunities and other relevant policies. SKILLS AND BEHAVIOURS (our Values in Practice): Accountability: Holds self-accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values Ambition: Sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages their team to do the same Collaboration: Approachable, good listener, builds and maintains effective relationships Creativity: Develops and encourages new and innovative solutions Integrity: Honest , encourages openness and transparency, builds trust and confidenceQUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE AND ATTRIBUTESEssential: • Degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management or related field. • 5 Years Field based and Hands On experience in supply chain management in an environment including complex procurement, transport and distribution, warehouse and stock management. • Experience in vehicle and fleet management, Distributions of NFI’s and food & Medical Supply Chain Management • Experience of building and developing the capacity of logistics staff. • Good People Management Skills and objective in Performance Management Conversations with Excellent interpersonal and team skills • Excellent Microsoft Applications Skills • Fluency in written and spoken English and Arabic including the ability to effectively motivate people and to diplomatically manage the relationship with local partners and different authorities • Commitment to and understanding of the organization’s aims, values and principlesDesirable • Other language would be an asset, • Eligible and willing to travel to project areas • Relevant qualifications or training courses. Save the Children does not charge any fees or request any form of payment at any stage of the recruitment process. How to applySupply Chain Coordinator-National-Damascus - SCI Career Site Careers

The purpose of this RFI is to gather information on: Availability of qualified GEDSI consultants and consulting firms; Relevant experience and technical capabilities; Service delivery models; Indicative market rates for GEDSI consulting services; and Market trends and regional expertise. This RFI is issued solely for market research and planning purposes and does not constitute a commitment to procure services, issue a Request for Proposal (RFP), or award a contract.| 2. Background World Vision seeks to strengthen GEDSI integration across programs, operations, organizational systems, policy implementation, capacity development initiatives, and strategic projects within the East Asia region. To support future planning and sourcing decisions, World Vision is undertaking a market assessment of GEDSI consulting services available within Southeast/South Asia. 3. Eligibility Requirements Have a minimum of five (5) years of GEDSI-related consulting experience; Have completed at least two (2) GEDSI assignments within Southeast/South Asia during the past five years; Demonstrate the ability to provide services remotely and/or travel within the region when required. Preferrably based in SouthEast/SouthAsia 4. Scope of Services (Indicative) The consultant may be requested to provide some or all of the following services: GEDSI strategy development and advisory services Technical review of projects and proposals Development of GEDSI tools, frameworks, and guidance documents Capacity building and training Facilitation of workshops and learning events GEDSI assessments, audits, and evaluations Integration of GEDSI into organizational processes Development of monitoring indicators and reporting frameworks Coaching and mentoring of staff This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information-gathering and market research purposes. World Vision is under no obligation to proceed with any procurement process or contract award as a result of this RFI. Information received through this process may be used to: Assess market capacity and capability; Benchmark pricing and service models; Evaluate procurement options; Inform future sourcing decisions; and Determine whether a competitive procurement process will be undertaken. Submission of a response does not create any contractual relationship between World Vision and the respondent. title: Venezuela Earthquake Response Manager- Readvertised
description: Countries: Colombia, Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of)                                       Organization: HelpAge International                                                                                         Closing date: 2 Sep 2026                                         Location: Venezuela, with flexibility to be based either in-country or in a nearby regional hub. Department: Programme Support Reports to (Line Manager): Head of Programme Support Grade: UK Salary Grade D or its equivalent based on the cost of living in the country of hire Contract Type: 12 months, Fixed term  About HelpAge HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience. Venezuela Earthquake Crisis On 24 June, two consecutive earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 struck north-central Venezuela at around 18:00 local time, followed by more than 130 aftershocks. The most affected areas are La Guaira, Caracas/Capital District, Miranda, Carabobo, and Yaracuy, with La Guaira reported as the area of most severe humanitarian impact. The earthquake has compounded the chronic deterioration of Venezuela's critical infrastructure, affecting transport networks, electricity, water systems, telecommunications, and public services. Damage to health facilities has further strained an already fragile health system, reducing access to emergency care, disrupting the continuity of treatment for chronic conditions, and limiting the availability of mental health and psychosocial support services at a time of increased demand. We are seeking a passionate, professional and experienced candidate to support our response to the Venezuela earthquake crisis, someone who thrives in collaborating with others (inside HelpAge International and beyond) and who can work in agile ways and across boundaries. About the Job The Venezuela Earthquake Response Manager will be responsible for the overall management of the Humanitarian response programme in Venezuela, which will be implemented by local partners, and will work closely with relevant members of the Programme Support and other Teams engaged with this emergency. There will be a strong focus on promoting the inclusion of older people in the emergency response and engaging in advocacy, as well as supporting roll out of training and guidance to make that happen. We are looking for someone skilled in program design and implementation, proposal preparation (with support from humanitarian staff), partner capacity building and support, quality assurance and monitoring, donor and stakeholder representation. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities Develop overall programmatic response and support 2-5 local implementing partners in programme start-up/scale up in response to the catastrophic earthquake in Venezuela. Oversee the programme management of humanitarian partner-led response, in line with Humanitarian Inclusion Standards with a focus on older people, in earthquake affected communities Monitor the quality of the humanitarian response, supporting implementing partners, making recommendations for change where needed to improve the impact on the lives of older people Work closely with the implementing partner organisations, including building their capacity, to ensure a high quality, age-friendly, inclusive, coordinated response Identify and develop new funding opportunities and project partnerships to build a humanitarian portfolio of work and increase the impact for older people in the response. Lead coordination between local implementing partners, HelpAge global teams and supporting members / donors With support from MEAL colleagues, lead on Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning for the response, tracking progress, sharing and utilizing related information, data, learning and evidence across the organisation and externally Ensure security of all staff and assets and compliance with external standards and internal requirements Act as primary representative with host governments, other officials in charge, donors, clusters, UN agencies and other International and national NGOs With the HelpAge Global Communications Manager be the primary spokesperson for HelpAge International on the ground which may include various media. Skills and experience required You will be someone with: Extensive experience managing complex multi-sector programs in an acute emergency situation Experience managing multi-donor funded projects including experience working with key emergency donors such as DEC, ECHO, Appeal funds, Trust and Foundations Demonstrable experience in leadership and programme management with local partners and geographically dispersed teams and in challenging humanitarian contexts. Familiarity with the Cluster system and its various areas of focus, with preferable experience in Protection and Inclusion promotion. Substantial experience in all aspects of Project Cycle Management with particular focus on proposal development, quality assurance, monitoring, Excellent interpersonal skills and a demonstrated ability to lead effectively in insecure environments An ability to represent HelpAge with traditional and non-traditional partners, donors and networks. Extensive knowledge of humanitarian principles, standards and human rights. Experienced in strengthening and supporting staff and national partner capacity An ability to travel, occasionally at short notice. title: DIRECTOR, COUNTRY - (5432)-Ethiopia
description: Country: Ethiopia                                       Organization: International Medical Corps                                                                       Closing date: 11 Nov 2026                                         DIRECTOR, COUNTRY - (5432) Job Title Director, Country Location Ethiopia - ET (Primary) Category Programs Date Needed By 12/1/2026 Program Description (Background) Job Description JOB SUMMARY: The Country Director is directly responsible for the overall strategic planning, human resources, program design and implementation, program support operations, finance, administration, safety and security monitoring and evaluation supervision, expansion/development, and required reporting for the country program. The Country Director plays a strong leadership role through a high level of strategic leadership and effective advocacy. The Country Director sets direction, leads, maintains team morale, safety and welfare, and manages resources while maintaining oversight and accountability. This role is ultimately accountable for all aspects of the country projects and ensuring that organizational setup is adapted to the operational context. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation. MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES Program Management Develop country specific strategic plan and proposals for programs in line with IMC’s global operational framework, considering country priority needs and in collaboration with country Senior Management Team (SMT). Coordinate with headquarters and country departments to design and implement high-quality programs, ensuring all programs are completed within time, within budget, achieving program objectives and in line with International Medical Corps principles, values, minimum standards, policies and strategic plans. Work closely with partners to identify a strategy for the maintaining and strengthening essential services and systems. Structure the country team for efficient operations and for accurate and timely collaboration and communication with headquarters, including the preparation and presentation of achievement of indicator targets, budget expenditure and procurement plans for monthly country-pipeline calls. Participate in writing and reviewing proposal applications. When applicable, provide technical inputs and assistance to programs with particular reference to financial management and reporting systems. Ensure Country Office participation in UN Clusters or other relevant coordination and other high level and operational coordination to ensure country programs are playing a vital role and to secure required support from the cluster coordination mechanism and the UN funding instruments such as CERF, CHF, etc. Coordinate and lead monthly pipelines review and follow on adequation between spending and program implementation. Report regularly to headquarters, providing timely updates of all operational situational and project management developments. Ensure monitoring, evaluation and reporting on all program activities and progress to headquarter office and donors. Compliance Oversee program operations and reporting, ensuring compliance with agency technical standards, policies and procedures, donor regulations and local laws. Facilitate investigations on violations of policies as appropriate. Oversee the preparation of annual work plans and budgets. Ensure compliance with local labor, NGO and technicality laws or present concerns to Senior Director / HQ Legal. Roll out protection risk assessment across all the projects and implement subsequent action plans. Program Development Develop a clear funding/resources mobilization strategy. Maintaining and expanding the country donor and financial portfolio based on the needs. Pursue new sources of donor funding and maintain adequate donor funding levels to sustain identified program and support activities, while meeting IMC technical standards and organizational policies, ensuring staff wellbeing. Leadership in proposal design and development, ensuring timely submission and providing inputs when applicable. Remaining aware of donor funding intention. Establish country partnerships to allow for collective organizations efforts through consortia. Human Resources Oversee the recruitment and selection of relevant qualified field staff, recommend promotions, disciplinary action and termination of staff in consultation with supervisors. Collaborate with security team in country to maintain security of staff in the field locations. When needed, make site visits to facilities to provide operational support to field site staff and ensure programs are being conducted timely and according to project plan. Plan for and manage any program critical incident including medical evacuation Maintain open lines of communications with all field staff. Sign all contracts for employment. Training/ Capacity Building Determine training needs for the field staff in coordination with relevant supervisors. Ensure senior national staff are trained to increase their responsibilities in order to build capacity and ensure sustainability of programs. Represent and plan for professional development for expat and national staff. Working Relationships Maintain frequent communication with direct supervisor to ensure program activities and objectives are communicated. Work with Senior Management Team (SMT) to ensure the coordination of programs. When possible, ensure representation of the organization at task force meetings, assessment missions, camp coordination meetings, UN coordination meetings, INGO coordination meetings. Interface with national government and relevant agencies to ensure mutual understanding of programs and maximize resource distribution and allocation of available funds. Ensure Source and lobby for resources for staff wellbeing. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning Overall responsibility for ensuring mission’s commitments towards donors and IMC’s requirements on Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (M/E) requirements. Integrate M/E into country strategies, frameworks, policies and plans. Include M/E related roles and responsibilities to all staff who are responsible for program management and implementation. Direct country level management to adequately budget for M/E activities across all grants. Ensures country level Community Based Feedback and Response Mechanism (CBFRM) procedure is in place, functioning, and adequately resourced. Ensures all highly sensitive complaints and feedback from the CBFRM are addressed and closed appropriately. Raises profile/awareness and importance of M/E with other senior management members through routine review and briefing sessions. Representation Represent the organization and liaise with local and national authorities, UN, NGO, and donor agencies, to promote the organization’s programs, facilitate successful coordination of activities and ensure transparency and accountability to all stakeholders. Serve as the principal liaison with Donors on matters related to the program to ensure financial and programmatic accountability to Donors. Establish and update contact details of potential Donors in-country. Participate in Donor meetings and communicate relevant information to HQ. Work with key Donor Staff to develop and maintain optimum financial and programmatic relationship Ensure maximum visibility of the Agency amongst the NGO community. Lead the production of reports and ensure the timeliness and accuracy of information provided, as well ensuring confidentiality of sensitive information. Contribute to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of the organizations Code of Conduct, ethics, values and standpoint with regard to internal and external actors. Security The Country Director is ultimately responsible for the security management of staff, operations, assets and directs country-specific response to security threats and incidents, up to and including management of evacuation. Monitor security level in collaboration with Country Security Management and consult with the HQ Global Security Senior Management to upgrade or downgrade level. Responsible for ensuring that Incident Report Forms are completed and submitted to HQ Security in a timely manner. Responsible for ensuring all staff are given a security briefing, and required documentation upon entry into the country. Ensure application and compliance of security protocols and policies. In cooperation with the Security Management, monitor the security situation and inform the HQ Security Management through weekly security reports. Ensure that country security guidelines, SOP’s and policies are updated twice annually (July 31 and January 31) including contingency planning for evacuation, in accordance with agency protocols and respected by all staff. Ensure adequate security funding is budgeted. Nominate security focal points at each operational site in country. Ensure Security staff in country are collecting and documenting local security related information (social and political context, external players, presence/reasons for conflict, military developments, political economy of armed groups), and communicating to the HQ Global Security Senior Management. Establish a reliable communication chain to disperse important information, whereby once the CD communicates a message, it is systematically passed on from one person to the next, with each person knowing who they are responsible for informing. (phone tree). Collaborate with local agencies to aid with security management. Perform other duties as assigned. Equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate. Typically, 12+ years proven progressive and significant experience in humanitarian programs and/or emergency response, mainly in the health or related field (Health policy, health reforms); including 10+ years of project management experience (management, planning, staff development and training), skills in emergency/ development programs; including 5+ years of experience in a senior-level management position in a field-based post. Financial management acumen, including managing budgets, banking activities, contracts and negotiations. Experience managing procurement and logistical procedures and policies. Knowledge in program sustainability and capacity building, public private partnerships and project monitoring and evaluation (both quantitative and qualitative methods). Strong writing, presentation and program development skills. Extensive fundraising and representational experience. Proven capabilities in leadership required. Strong negotiation, interpersonal and organization skills. Our Code of Conduct and Ethics and Whistleblower Policy prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. description: Country: Vanuatu                                       Organization: DT Global                                                                                         Closing date: 10 Sep 2026                                         Program Background Pacific Australia Skills is a significant Australian investment which stands to make a major contribution to supporting social and economic growth in the region through strengthening the skills and training sector across the Pacific and Timor-Leste. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of 17 years of Australian Government support for skills and training in the Pacific and TImor-Leste. About DT Global Asia Pacific At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact. The role supports the operationalising of the Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan, as well as effective implementation of Pacific Australia Skills safeguarding strategy in line with Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) Safeguarding Policies (Child Protection and PSEAH), DT Global safeguarding frameworks, and relevant national and international standards. To enhance skills at the country level, the adviser will facilitate professional development in safeguarding and inclusive approaches for Pacific Australia Skills staff, partners and other stakeholders in Vanuatu. The role also supports the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) and Communications team to ensure inclusion is embedded within MEL systems, communication products and incorporated into country plans. Roles and ResponsibilitiesInclusion: Pacific Australia Skills uses the term Inclusion to describe its work in advancing Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI). The Inclusion and Safeguarding Adviser will: Support the implementation of the Pacific Australia Skills Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan across Vanuatu. Work with program staff and partners to embed gender equality, disability equity and social inclusion (GEDSI) principles into program design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. Support partner organisations to identify and address barriers to participation for women, people with disabilities, youth and other underrepresented groups. Facilitate inclusion awareness activities, training and professional development opportunities for Pacific Australia Skills, Vanuatu staff and partners. Facilitate Inclusion orientation and onboarding sessions for new short-term and long-term Pacific Australia Skills, Vanuatu staff and experts. Support the development of inclusive training approaches, resources and learning environments. Assist the MEL team to ensure inclusion indicators, data collection and reporting processes capture meaningful information on participation and outcomes. Support the communications team to ensure communication products promote inclusive and accessible practices and positively represent diverse participants. Contribute to stakeholder engagement and partnerships with organisations working in gender equality, disability inclusion and social inclusion. Safeguarding Support the implementation of Pacific Australia Skills safeguarding requirements in Vanuatu, ensuring alignment with DFAT and DT Global requirements, including Child Protection (CP), Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), and broader duty of care obligations. Assist in promoting safeguarding awareness across the program using clear, practical, and inclusive approaches Support integration of safeguarding requirements into program activities, ensuring accessibility, inclusion, and safe participation Lead the conducting of safeguarding due diligence and capacity assessments of partners and service providers in Vanuatu. Support safeguarding inductions, training and awareness sessions for Pacific Australia Skills staff, consultants and partners. Maintain accurate, secure, and confidential safeguarding records in relevant systems. Support monitoring of safeguarding risks and implementation of mitigation measures in line with Do No Harm and risk management principles. The CoP will focus on practitioner support, learning, innovation and coordination. Support the Partnership Manager and country team to embed inclusion and safeguarding requirements across all country partnerships, initiatives and activities. Ensure compliance with mandatory inclusion and safeguarding procedures, briefing sessions, and environmental assessment in line with project operational plans and sectoral training measure. Contribute to work planning, activity design, reporting and partner engagement processes. Support coordination with regional Inclusion and Safeguarding teams to ensure alignment with Pacific Australia Skills approaches and standards. Assist with the preparation of reports, case studies and lessons learned relating to inclusion and safeguarding outcomes. Read more about this company Head of Pharmacy Operations and Clinical Procurement - Equity Afya Job Type Full Time Qualification BA/BSc/HND , MBA/MSc/MA , Professional Certificate Experience 8 years Location Nairobi Job Field Pharmaceutical The Role Purpose Reporting to the Chief Pharmacist, the Head of Pharmacy Operations & Clinical Procurement is responsible for providing strategic leadership for pharmaceutical operations, clinical procurement, supply chain management, and business growth initiatives across the network. The role is accountable for developing strategic partnerships, negotiating supplier contracts, ensuring regulatory compliance, and guaranteeing the continuous availability of pharmaceuticals and other clinical supplies while optimizing inventory costs, supporting clinic profitability, and maintaining high standards of patient care The Key Responsibilities Strategy and Leadership: Develop, implement, and evaluate long-term and short-term strategic plans to advance pharmaceutical services in alignment with EQA’s mission and objectives. Provide leadership and direction for the pharmacy section across multiple sites or facilities. Represent pharmacy interests at the management level and participate in organizational decision-making. Manage key strategic partnerships to optimize the performance of the pharmacy section. Collaborate with the clinical team, Franchisees and other stakeholders to conduct business research and align business needs with the overall EQA goals. Partnerships and Business Support: Grow Pharmacy revenue, market share, brand growth & visibility. Proactively identify potential strategic partnerships for business growth and expansion. Manage relationships with Pharmacy accrediting and regulatory bodies to enhance partnership and collaboration. Serve as subject matter expert for drug procurement, medical devices and equipment and service providers related to pharmaceutical regulatory and donors’ requirements. Provide timely, accurate and credible reports on the status of the pharmacy section. Lead the identification, development, and management of strategic partnerships with pharmaceutical manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, donors, and other healthcare supply partners to support business growth, affordability, and supply continuity. Negotiate and oversee commercial agreements, service level agreements (SLAs), and supply contracts to achieve optimal pricing, quality, availability, and value for the organization. Ensure effective supplier performance management through regular review of supplier service levels, contract compliance, pricing competitiveness, and product availability. Establish and maintain strategic partnerships that strengthen access to pharmaceuticals, laboratory commodities, medical consumables, medical devices, and other clinical supplies across the network Business Planning and Budgeting: Develop and manage Pharmacy department budget, optimize resource allocation, and oversee cost-containment strategies without compromising quality of care. Conduct internal and external periodic performance reviews against key metrices to monitor the performance of the pharmacy section and take prompt action to maintain quality service. Clinical Supply Chain Management: Optimize purchasing of pharmaceutical supplies and drug formulary decisions to ensure affordability of medication without compromising quality. Negotiate favourable contracts and partnerships with pharmaceutical suppliers and vendors. Support the procurement processes of pharmaceuticals & clinical items for the medical centres. Identify & leverage on opportunities for continuous quality improvement and process reengineering to optimize operational efficiency and patient care at the Equity Afya facilities. Establish EQA Formulary for Pharmaceuticals, Non-Pharms, Lab and Other Medical supplies. Develop and implement EQA annual Procurement Plan for Pharmaceuticals, Non-Pharms, Lab and Other Medical supplies. Develop, implement, and continuously optimize inventory management systems and controls across the EQA network to ensure consistent availability of pharmaceuticals, laboratory commodities, nutrition products, medical consumables, medical devices, and other clinical supplies while maintaining optimal inventory holding costs and minimizing expiries, wastage, and stockouts. Manage end to end supply chain process for pharmaceuticals, nutrition products, medical devices and medical equipment requirements for EQA Kenya & the francophone countries that EQA operates in. Support in the development of processes to ensure compliance related to key supply chain requirements such as quality control, cold chain storage and distribution. Lead strategic supplier relationship management to continually identify process improvements and cost reduction opportunities. Clinical Compliance, Risk and Process Improvement Develop, implement, and maintain a robust quality management system for the pharmacy section, in compliance with relevant regulations and guidelines. Drive initiatives to enhance operational efficiency through technology, process improvement, and innovation. Ensure that Equity Afya network adheres to existing regulations and guidelines of the Pharmacy & Poisons Board (PPB) and other relevant regulators within the region. Audit compliance of the facilities as per approved checklist and report to management any unfavourable trends in unmet indicators for timely remedial action. Perform risk assessments to identify potential quality issues and develop strategies to mitigate them. Provide leadership in clinical pharmacy services, including medication therapy management (MTM), drug information, and patient counselling. Monitor and improve medication-use processes to ensure patient safety and optimize therapeutic outcomes. Identify & leverage opportunities for continuous quality improvement and process reengineering to optimize operational efficiency and patient care at the Equity Afya facilities. Accountable for ensuring uninterrupted availability of all pharmaceuticals and clinical supplies required to support safe patient care, operational efficiency, and revenue generation across the network. Establish inventory planning, forecasting, replenishment, and stock optimization strategies that balance service levels, working capital requirements, and clinic profitability. Monitor inventory turnover, stock holding days, expiry rates, procurement savings, and supply chain performance to drive continuous improvement and cost optimization. Develop and implement supply continuity and risk mitigation plans to address supply disruptions, supplier shortages, and market volatility. People Management Develop and cascade goals and Key performance indicators to ensure individual members of your team meet their performance expectations. Build and mentor a high-performing leadership team within the pharmacy department. Promote a culture of excellence, accountability, and professional development among pharmacy staff. Develop and implement training programs to enhance patient education regarding medications and treatment plans. Core Accountabilities and Deliverables Implement a standard medicines optimization plan across all franchise sites with ≥95% formulary adherence and annual review updates. Achieve ≥90% compliance on quarterly clinical audits and close 100% of corrective actions within 30 days network‑wide. Deliver quarterly training/coaching sessions for all franchise pharmacy teams and maintain ≥85% staff competence scores. Maintain availability of essential pharmaceuticals and clinical supplies at ≥95%, achieve stockout rates of <1%, and maintain stock variance rates within approved thresholds. Maintain stock holding days ≤30 days, across the Franchisee network Achieve 50% annual cost savings through optimized purchasing and reduce wastage to <2% across the franchise network. Secure ≥80% franchise participation in centralized procurement and reduce lead times for essential items to ≤7 days. Roll out the network digital inventory system to 100% of franchise facilities with ≥85% reporting compliance and pilot at least two innovations per year. Deliver inventory optimization initiatives that improve inventory turnover, reduce working capital tied in stock, minimize expiries and wastage, and contribute positively to clinic profitability. Key Decisions Made by the Job-Holder (Not Recommendations) and How Often Sets the overall strategic direction, growth priorities, and geographic expansion of the outpatient health facilities network. Approves pharmaceutical strategy, formularies, and procurement frameworks. Sets pharmaceutical quality, safety, and compliance standards across the network. Authorizes supplier selection, major pharmaceutical contracts, and risk mitigation actions. Acts as the final escalation point for significant pharmaceutical, regulatory, or safety incidents. Recommends pharmacy-related investments, systems, and innovations to executive leadership. Complexity Expected in the Role (E.g. Multiple Countries, Cross-Functional Responsibilities, Delivering Through Other Third Parties) Ensuring compliance and quality in franchise pharmacies without direct authority. Managing regulatory variability across the network. Balancing cost control with medicine availability and quality. Protecting brand and patient safety in decentralized operations. Driving adoption of standardized systems and protocols across diverse operators. Balancing Vendor needs, and the franchise business needs. Critical Relationships/Stakeholders/Contacts Internal: The EQA senior EXCO Team, External: Franchisees, Regulators, Government Agencies, Suppliers, Public Media/Press Qualifications Key Technical Skills & Leadership Competencies Ability to articulate the vision, expectations, and strategies clearly across multiple levels. A track record of high performance in the health sector. Ability to define long-term strategy, growth priorities, and market expansion plans. Strong financial acumen and understanding of budgeting, forecasting, profitability, and cost management. Understanding of Pharmacy governance, patient safety, and healthcare compliance. High level of commercial experience, exposure and hands on skills in Pharmaceuticals. Ability to lead system, formulary, and process changes across the network. Skilled in building capable teams and upholding professional and ethical standards Possess the ability to build nurture business relationships with key business stakeholders and have distinguished hands-on operational skills. Strong expertise in pharmaceutical and clinical supply procurement, strategic sourcing, contract negotiation, supplier relationship management, and supply chain optimization to ensure cost-effective, quality-assured, and uninterrupted availability of healthcare commodities. Experience Requirements At least 8 years of progressive leadership experience in pharmacy, healthcare, or supply chain operations, with a proven track record of leading high-performing teams. Experience managing pharmaceutical services, medicines optimization, and clinical governance within healthcare organizations. Experience overseeing multi-site, franchise, or multi-country pharmacy operations is highly desirable. Demonstrated experience in procurement, supply chain management, inventory optimization, and supplier relationship management. Proven track record in regulatory compliance, quality assurance, and audit management. Experience driving operational efficiency, cost optimization, and financial performance improvement initiatives. Experience implementing and utilizing pharmacy, inventory, ERP, or digital health systems to improve operational outcomes. Strong stakeholder management experience, including engagement with regulators, healthcare providers, suppliers, insurers, and senior leadership Academic Qualifications and Certifications Bachelor's Degree in Pharmacy from a recognized institution. Registered Pharmacist with a valid practicing license. Master's degree in Pharmacy, Public Health, Healthcare Management, Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, or a related field will be an added advantage. Professional certifications in supply chain management, project management, quality management, or leadership are desirable Check how your CV aligns with this job Method of Application Interested and qualified? title: Deputy Field Coordinator for Programs Deir ez-Zor – SYRIA
description: Country: Syrian Arab Republic                                       Organization: Première Urgence Internationale                                                                       Closing date: 10 Sep 2026                                         Fixed-term contract: 12 months from 14/09/2026 Deadline for application: 10/09/2026 PUI all around the world With its 40 years of experience, Première Urgence Internationale : Supports close to 6 millions beneficiaries With more than 100 millions € yearly budget Present in 22 countries, on 5 continents Thanks to the work and commitment of : More than 2000 national staffs Around 200 expatriates from 45 different nationalities And 90 employees at HQ PUI works in 10 areas of intervention and distinguishes itself by the implementation of an integrated approach in its response. This method aims to identify and understand the needs of all those affected by a crisis. Our teams come together to bring a rapid global response to the basic needs of populations affected by humanitarian crises to help them regain independence and dignity. Learn more on our history, our values, our areas of intervention. What about the Deputy Field Coordinator for Programs ? As Deputy Field Coordinator for Programs, you will be responsible for monitoring the effective implementation of the program at the base level and for monitoring PUI’s contractual obligations and reporting. You will also be responsible for representing PUI on programmatic issues to other humanitarian actors and to technical and administrative state authorities at the local level. For this purpose, you will be responsible for: Strategic Development, follow-up of operations and reporting: You will coordinate the project teams through the program managers and ensure the proper implementation of the operational and qualitative aspects of the programs (objectives monitoring, respect of deadlines and budgetary deadlines, quality control, team synergy in accordance with the contractual documents and in compliance with PUI policies and procedures. You will ensure that contractual obligations are respected and coordinate the writing of reports. You will ensure that the programs developed are in line with PUI’s mandate and strategy and will propose new interventions according to the evolution of the humanitarian situation in the region. MEAL: You will coordinate the MEAL department and ensure the implementation of the activities of this department as well as the interactions with the programs and the design of relevant tools. Representation: You will participate in technical forums (working groups) at the local level in collaboration with the project leaders. You will assist the Field Co in coordination meetings between NGOs or with political and administrative authorities. Human Resources: You will be the direct supervisor of the project managers in this base and will ensure that appropriate support and capacity building is provided to senior program staff. Logistics and Administration: You will support the project managers in supervising the logistical and administrative tasks of the projects with the support of the logistics and administration departments. The challenges that await you Challenging living conditions: Compared with other PUI bases in Syria, Deir ez-Zor is a relatively difficult duty station in terms of access to services and general living conditions. Limited lifestyle and leisure options: Social, recreational, and leisure activities are very limited compared with other locations in Syria. Complex community engagement and acceptance: The context requires careful community engagement and strong attention to acceptance, particularly due to past and ongoing tensions between different communities and groups. Geographically dispersed activities: Projects are implemented across several locations, with significant distances between some intervention sites. This requires regular field travel and strong planning and coordination. What you will need to succeed Training: You hold a Master‘s degree in a field related to project management, international development and/or social sciences. Experience: You are strengthened by minimum 2 years of experience in project management and/or monitoring, and at least 2 years as a humanitarian project manager. You already worked with Première Urgence Internationale? It would be a definite asset! Skills: You master the methodology and the project management cycle, you have competence in studies and diagnosis. If you have knowledge of humanitarian donors, of database management and statistical software packages, it would be appreciated. Qualities: You have strong leadership and management skills, the ability to make decisions, a sense of analysis (discernment, pragmatism) and synthesis. You are a good communicator, both in writing and orally. You demonstrate organization, rigor, flexibility, and a strong commitment to support/build capacity of project leaders. You also have a good resilience to stress. Languages: English has no secrets for you! All the better, it is mandatory for this position. If you speak Arabic and/or French, it would be a definite asset. A word from the manager « We are looking for a candidate with a strong programmatic background and solid field experience, combined with strong leadership and management skills. title: Programme Manager - Operations and Grants
description: Country: Netherlands                                       Organization: CARE Nederland                                                                       Closing date: 1 Sep 2026                                         About CARE CARE is a global leader in fighting poverty and delivering innovative solutions to empower communities. With a mission to save lives, defeat poverty, and achieve social justice, CARE works in over 100 countries, focusing on gender equality, sustainable development, and resilience. We do this by working for the empowerment of women and communities that are disproportionately affected by climate change, natural disasters or conflict. In doing so, we create structural change, in close collaboration with partners, governments and communities. The CASCADE programme (CAtalyzing Strengthened policy aCtion for heAlthy Diets and resiliencE) aims to improve food security and contribute to the reduction of malnutrition of at least 5 million people, with a focus on women of reproductive age and children in Benin, Ethiopia, Kenya, Mozambique, Nigeria, and Uganda. Using an advocacy-centered approach that galvanizes government, businesses, and communities, the programme has 2 Strategic Objectives: to increase access to and consumption of healthy diets, to increase the resilience of households to economic and climate-related shocks Efforts across the 6 countries are contextually driven and are 1) strengthening food systems and nutrition policy and government accountability for financing and implementing these; 2) re-engineering markets and mobilizing private sector; 3) mitigating the effects of negative cultural norms and practices on nutritional well-being and diets of women of reproductive age and children under 5 years of age; 4) strengthening capacities of mothers and families of young children to access healthy diets year round; and, 5) systematizing data and learning for policy and decision-making at all levels of government. CASCADE is 4.5-year programme, now in its third year, funded by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. The programme consortium is led by CARE Netherlands with participation from CARE USA and one major international partner, the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN). Country programmes also partner with a range of different local partners to enhance sustainability of interventions. Job Overview The Operations and Grants Programme Manager supports the overall operations of the CASCADE consortium, including ensuring appropriate systems and processes for grants and contract management, compliance, risk monitoring and management appropriate for a complex, multi-country programme. Given the timeline of the CASCADE programme cycle, the priority tasks for this position will focus on financial, administration and contractual close out across the six countries, and of global operations for the 3 consortium partners. Key Responsibilities 1. Operations, project and grant management – 60% For the consortium: Serve as the focal point for project operations and grants management for six country teams, collaborating closely with the GAIN Programme Lead. Develop and manage consortium trackers to keep the overview for operational and close-out plans and deliverables, procurement, sub-grants, budgets, and internal / external consortium deadlines, etc. Together with the Project Controller, track country expenditures, review budget vs. actual reports with country programmes on a timely basis linking spending to workplans, and support country teams on projections, accruals, and close-out planning. Coordinate the process of annual work plans and budgets, and annual reporting with guidance from the Sr. Technical Programmes Manager. Support the Sr. Technical Programmes Manager in ensuring technical guidance and decisions are adhered to. Together with the GAIN Programme Lead and Programme Associate, coordinate regular reviews and updates on country-specific risk management matters and bring to the attention of the PMU. Coordinate award start-up and close-out and the onboarding and phase-out of country office staff within the global consortium. For CARE: Support contracting between CARE NL and the six CARE country offices and sub-granting for CARE country offices; Coordinate CARE global procurement for the programme where needed and support the major procurement processes in the countries of implementation through the respective partners; Ensure that CARE internal systems are complete and up-to-date, including completing the annual PIIRS reviews in coordination with MEAL and TA staff and keeping the country descriptions in Promeva updated; Coordinate programme close-out processes with CARE offices, including with local partner organizations, vendors, asset disposition, and staff phase-out, etc. Support the Project Director and Project Controller on updates to contracts with consortium partners and sub-contractors, as needed. 2. Compliance and risk management – 15% With guidance from the Project Director, follow-up on donor requirements and compliance, local regulations, and financial and administrative processes, working closely with the GAIN Programme Lead, GAIN Programme Associate, and Financial Controller; Set up and manage trackers and systems for documentation and monitoring of key operations risks and indicators for the CASCADE consortium to support compliance and risk management, with a focus on programme close-out processes; Support country teams in the operational aspects of adaptive management, problem-solving, and programme close-out. Programme Associate, Project Controller, Sr. Technical Programme Manager, etc., to coordinate where required. 3. Oversee consortium administration – 10% Supervise and coach the consortium Project Officer, who is responsible for consortium administration work such as scheduling, updating and maintaining team calendars and systems, supporting scheduling, etc. Support the Project Officer to ensure all meetings comply with programme standards, such as ensuring meeting agendas are set and shared in advance, notetaking roles are assigned and notes shared within in a timely manner. Responsibilities and timelines for follow-up should also be set at the end of each meeting and followed up on, accordingly. 4. CARE NL linking and other tasks – 15% Serve as CARE NL portfolio focal person for Kenya and Mozambique Country Offices, as needed; Keep the relevant CARE NL portfolio manager for Benin, Ethiopia, Nigeria, and Uganda regularly informed and coordinate around any issues relevant to the country office relationship or country context / risks; Take part in Sustainable Development Team meetings and leverage CASCADE experience to support CARE NL learning and programme development; Other tasks, as assigned by Project Director and Sr. Technical Programme Manager. Contacts The Operations & Grants Programme Manager for CASCADE is managed by the Project Director and is a member of the SD Team. The PM works closely with the Sr. Technical Programme Manager, GAIN Programme Lead, GAIN Programme Associate, and Financial Controller. The Operations & Grants Programme Manager supervises one Project Officer who supports administration for operations, IT platforms (e.g. SharePoint), KML, and for the Project Director and Sr. Technical Programme Manager. What do you bring to the table? At least 5 years’ experience supporting large, international grants and contracts and managing compliance and risk; Past experience ensuring donor compliance of a consortium programme of high complexity, preferably funded by Netherlands MFA; Experience developing trackers and tools for use internally and with the donor; Ability to manage multiple, competing priorities; Experience working closely with finance staff to ensure financial administration; Experience working with multi-country teams remotely, and ability to cultivate a strong team dynamic across cultures, languages, time zones, and skill sets; Professional-level French writing and speaking skills are required in this role; Excellent written and verbal communication skills; Familiarity with the Office 365 suite of tools, including Teams and SharePoint; Academic work and thinking level; Affinity or experience with policy work and nutrition / food systems transformation, or related themes (e.g. agriculture, resilience, food security, community health, etc.); Willingness to travel to programme countries. CARE maintains a zero tolerance policy on sexual exploitation and abuse and child abuse and takes all concerns and complaints about sexual exploitation and abuse and child abuse involving CARE staff and related personnel seriously. What does CARE Nederland offer? An interesting position where taking initiative is stimulated. A gross monthly salary based on BBRA scale 10, classification depends on relevant working experience. One-year contract with possible extension. International informal work environment in which you work with colleagues from different backgrounds to achieve the goals of CARE Nederland. Open work culture characterized by weekly joint coffee moments and regular staff meetings. Location in the bustling heart of The Hague. Ready to apply? Are you interested in this position and do you meet the profile sought? Please send your application using the button below. The deadline to respond to this vacancy is 1 Sept 2026. For more information, please contact Sarah Harris EU work permit is a requirement for this position. As long as the vacancy is still visible, responding remains possible. Acquisition in response to this advertisement is not appreciated. How to applyProgramme Manager - Operations and Grants - Vacature

title: Program Manager II - BMU MEAL Manager (Filipino Nationals Preferred)
description: Country: Philippines                                       Organization: Catholic Relief Services                                                                       Closing date: 2 Sep 2026                                         About CRS Catholic Relief Services is the official international humanitarian agency of the Catholic community in the United States. CRS works to save, protect, and transform lives in need in around 100 countries, without regard to race, religion or nationality. CRS’ relief and development work is accomplished through programs of emergency response, agriculture, education, water and sanitation, climate resilience, disaster risk reduction, capacity strengthening, social cohesion and justice and health. CRS Philippines, established in 1945, is the longest running, continuous CRS country program in the world with extensive programming in emergency response and recovery, and disaster risk reduction, climate resilience and livelihoods. The Philippines country program has over 60 staff members spread across project locations. CRS Philippines is committed to collaborating with our strong network of church partners, national and subnational government agencies and secular NGOs throughout the country. In the North Pacific, CRS has a Program office in the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) implementing community-based disaster risk reduction, emergency response and early recovery projects. Currently, there are 14 staff members located in three islands in FSM, i.e. Pohnpei, Chuuk and Yap. Recently, Philippines and FSM were combined as one Business Management Unit (BMU) under the new Europe, Middle East and Asia (EMEA) regional structure. This integration envisions shared services and management oversight across the two countries, with Philippines as BMU lead country, having overall responsibility for MEAL, Finance, Human Resources, among others. Job Summary The Program Manager II - BMU MEAL Manager will lead and provide strategic direction of the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and learning for various projects implemented by CRS in the Philippines and FSM ensuring effective systems and processes are in place that support high-quality programming advancing Catholic Relief Services’ (CRS) work in serving the poor and vulnerable. The BMU MEAL manager will advance accountability and contribute to business development initiatives. The BMU MEAL Manager will be responsible for coordinating and supervising MEAL activities, working closely with CRS program teams and partner staff to develop and implement high-quality monitoring systems and tools for evidence-based monitoring of indicators. The BMU MEAL Manager will supervise project MEAL officers across the two countries. Support the project team in the design and implementation of vulnerability assessments, stakeholder mapping and analysis, gender analyses, and other pre-program data collection and analysis. Collect and analyze lessons learned and best practices from previous and ongoing programs capturing the impact of carbon sequestration activities to ensure they feed into program strategies as appropriate. Leverage lessons learned, best practices, program data, evaluations and other information to generate donor communication pieces, success stories, case studies and other high-quality, results-based documentation. Work with the senior management team to identify and pursue strategic opportunities for program expansion. MEAL Implementation Lead mandated evaluations, needs assessments, annual surveys, case studies and other research efforts and CRS global reporting requirements. Develop and manage the countrywide accountability tracking system across the BMU that supports project decision making and risk management. Ensure that transparent high-quality accountability mechanisms, including beneficiary feedback and response mechanisms, are in place and are regularly discussed at the appropriate level with necessary responses and feedback documented. Support learning-to-action events, cross learning and reflection sessions to systematically analyze data to promote adaptive management and to document and incorporate lessons learned into program design and implementation. Develop tailored MEAL operating manual to ensure complete, up-to-date, high quality MEAL system, containing essential data collection tools, data flow maps and analysis plans to address need-to-know information for program quality and donor reporting. Contribute to donor reports through high quality project data interpretation and report inputs and reviews. Ensure MEAL and program teams regularly review and adjust MEAL plans and tools as needed by the project context. Work with MEAL and IT staff / GKIM to maximize the value and utility of ICT4D in MEAL initiatives. MEAL Capacity Building Provide training, mentoring, and ongoing technical assistance to CRS program teams, MEAL teams and implementing partners in the Philippines and FSM to ensure effective implementation of MEAL methodologies and tools and high-quality data. Support partners to incorporate participatory methods into community-level MEAL systems and tools. Conduct field monitoring frequently with project teams and implementing partners. Conduct periodic data quality audits and provide technical assistance to address any issues identified. MEAL in Business Development Lead MEAL design for proposals by developing results frameworks, indicators, monitoring systems, and learning approaches aligned with donor and CRS requirements. Provide technical inputs to project design through contributions to theories of change, logframes, assessments, evidence generation, and measurement methodologies. Serve as the MEAL focal point during business development by drafting MEAL sections, developing required annexes, and ensuring accountability, learning, and data quality mechanisms are integrated into proposals. Additional experience may substitute for some education. Five years' experience working in a development setting preferably with an international NGO, with experience of progressively increasing MEAL responsibility in international development projects particularly in Landscape Management and Restoration, Climate Smart Agriculture or Sustainable Agriculture Practices or other relevant areas. At least three years of supervisory experience. Preferred Qualifications Demonstrated expertise in developing and operationalizing routine monitoring systems designed to track both output and outcome indicators (including work with logical frameworks and theories of change) Strong ICT4D skills and GIS mapping experience; familiarity donor (USG, FCDO, UN) MEAL guidelines and policies. Experienced in developing data quality assurance strategies, data management and data visualization, including proficiency in database development/management, Stata, SPSS, EPI-Info, Access, Excel and skills in analyzing, interpreting and communicating information to various stakeholders. Demonstrated expertise and experience in data utilization strategies and can creatively think about active data sharing techniques. Experience with facilitation, capacity strengthening and partnership building through formal and informal training, with the capacity to empower staff through opportunities for professional growth and development. Experience engaging with partner organizations and the Government of the Philippines at national and local levels. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make sound judgment and decisions and offer innovative solutions Strong relations management abilities. Ability to relate to people at all levels internally and externally. Strategic approach to relationships and ability to influence results. Consortium management experience preferred. Good presentation and facilitation skills Proactive, resourceful, solutions-oriented and results-oriented Experience using MS Windows and MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information management systems.
